sections.preamble: You are a coding assistant running inside pi, a coding agent harness. Help users inspect files, run commands, and modify code.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- write: Create or overwrite files
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use edit for targeted changes. Batch changes to one file in a single call.
- Each edits[].oldText must exactly and uniquely match the original file. Keep matches short and non-overlapping; merge nearby changes without including large unchanged regions.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

content.text: Generate an animated SVG of an anteater riding a unicycle while juggling bottles.

content.thinking:
**Designing Animated Anteater**

I'm currently focused on sketching out the core animation sequence. My priority is capturing that delightful, bouncy motion of the anteater on the unicycle, along with the fluid, rhythmic arc of the juggling bottles. I'm aiming for a visually engaging and memorable performance.

**Generating Animated SVG**

I'm refining the output strategy for the animated SVG. My current thinking leans towards directly embedding the complete, self-contained SVG within the response's code block, avoiding unsolicited file creation. This approach seems most aligned with typical coding assistant interactions and ensures the SVG is immediately accessible.

**Detailing Animation Cycles**

I'm fleshing out the mechanics of the anteater's cycling motion, focusing on synchronized pedal strokes, leg articulation, and subtle shifts in body balance to convey a sense of dynamic equilibrium. Simultaneously, I'm meticulously choreographing the three vibrant glass bottles, ensuring their arc, spin, and the classic three-ball cascade pattern are rendered with fluid, engaging realism.

I've begun mapping out the coordinate system and layering strategy. The `viewBox` will be set to `0 0 640 520`. For the background, I envision a warm, inviting circus or park scene with a soft radial gradient transitioning from `#FFF6E5` to `#FAD7A0` and `#F5B7B1`, suggesting a sunset glow. I'm planning a subtle pulsing shadow beneath the unicycle wheel to accentuate balance, and I've decided on animated ground markings—specifically, dashed lines scrolling from right to left—to enhance the perception of forward motion and the unicycle's smooth progression.

**Animating Wheel Motion**

I'm focusing on the unicycle wheel's rotation. It will spin clockwise, with its center at `(320, 405)`. The tire bottom will just kiss the ground at `Y=465`. I'm also detailing the spokes' rotation using `animateTransform` and planning the fork, seat post, and pedal mechanics now.

**Coordinating Crank and Leg**

I'm refining the leg animation to precisely mirror the pedal's movement. By synchronizing SMIL `<animate>` on leg `<path>` elements with the pedal's calculated 8-angle positions, I'm ensuring a natural and dynamic cycling motion from hip to pedal. This detailed approach will bring lifelike fluidity to the anteater's ride.

**Cycling Crank Synchronization**

I'm currently focused on calculating the precise knee joint coordinates for each of the eight pedal positions. This involves a two-bone inverse kinematics approach, accounting for thigh and shin lengths, to ensure natural leg articulation and a realistic cycling motion as the pedal moves through its arc.

**Calculating Knee Positions**

I'm refining the inverse kinematics for the anteater's leg. I've calculated specific knee joint coordinates for eight pedal positions, ensuring a natural articulation from hip to pedal as the cycle progresses.

**Calculating Leg Positions**

I've finalized the inverse kinematics, precisely calculating eight knee joint coordinates for each pedal position. This ensures a natural leg articulation, and I'm now selecting between a quadratic Bezier or a two-segment polyline for the leg's visual representation, opting for rounded strokes and a cute paw.

**Designing Anteater Details**

I'm detailing the anteater's appearance now, focusing on its iconic diagonal stripe and the massive, bushy tail that will sway for balance. The fur coloration and head shape are also coming into focus, aiming for a charming, recognizable giant anteater.

**Designing Anteater Details**

I'm now refining the anteater's expressive features. I'm planning a bright, forward-looking gaze with a hint of concentration, and I've decided to add a charming red bow tie and a jaunty circus cap for extra personality. My focus is on ensuring these details enhance the overall playful and engaging character.

**Adjusting Hand Positions**

I'm refining the anteater's hand placement for optimal juggling visibility. I've positioned the hands to create a wide, clear arc for the bottles, ensuring the entire juggling sequence remains easily readable and visually engaging directly in front of its snout.

**Juggling Three Bottles**

I'm focused on perfecting the three-bottle juggling cascade. I've defined the cycle timing with a period of 2.4 seconds, ensuring each bottle is staggered by 0.8 seconds. I'm also meticulously mapping out the figure-8 path using cubic Beziers, from the throw points to the apex and catch points.

**Completing Bottle Trajectories**

I'm now finalizing the individual bottle paths for the juggling sequence. I'm using cubic Beziers to meticulously map each throw, apex, and catch, ensuring a smooth figure-eight motion. I'm also experimenting with `keyTimes` and `keyPoints` to simulate natural acceleration and deceleration.

**Juggling Hand Synchronization**

I'm aligning the timing of the scoops between my hands. Each hand will alternate catching and throwing every 0.8 seconds, ensuring a continuous 2.4-second cycle. This creates a seamless, staggered effect for the juggling cascade, with each hand spending 40% of the cycle in the air and 10% in a scoop.

**Checking Bottle Timing**

I'm meticulously verifying the bottle timing. It appears my previous assessment of hand alternation was slightly off; each hand actually catches and throws every 0.8 seconds, with a 0.4-second offset between them, resulting in a continuous cascade.

**Synchronizing Hand and Bottle**

I'm refining the hand-to-bottle timing. I've synchronized the hand's scoop action with the bottle's catch point, ensuring each hand is in position precisely when the bottle arrives. This creates a perfect, continuous cascade rhythm.

**Verifying Rendering Logic**

I'm cross-referencing all SVG syntax and SMIL animation attributes for robust cross-browser rendering. My focus is ensuring seamless execution in Chrome, Firefox, and Safari, particularly regarding `path` usage in `animateMotion` and clean ID naming for `<defs>`. I'm also reviewing the `d` values for the leg animations across all frames.

**Verifying Pedal Mechanics**

I'm double-checking the crank arm and pedal animations for seamless integration. Each crank arm rotates 360 degrees around the center, synchronized with the pedal's circular path. I'm ensuring the pedal platform remains level as it orbits, and the front leg precisely mirrors these movements.

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 640 520" width="640" height="520" role="img" aria-label="Animated anteater riding a unicycle while juggling three bottles">
  <defs>
    <!-- Sky & stage gradients -->
    <linearGradient id="skyGrad" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#FFF5E1" />
      <stop offset="68%" stop-color="#FDE2B8" />
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#F7C59F" />
    </linearGradient>

    <radialGradient id="spotGrad" cx="50%" cy="46%" r="52%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#FFFFFF" stop-opacity="0.55" />
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#FFFFFF" stop-opacity="0" />
    </radialGradient>

    <linearGradient id="groundGrad" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#D99B66" />
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#B57242" />
    </linearGradient>

    <!-- Anteater fur gradients -->
    <linearGradient id="furMain" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="1">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#9A887C" />
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#6F5E53" />
    </linearGradient>

    <linearGradient id="furDark" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="1">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#6B5B51" />
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#4A3E37" />
    </linearGradient>

    <linearGradient id="tailGrad" x1="1" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#7A685D" />
      <stop offset="55%" stop-color="#574940" />
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#3E332C" />
    </linearGradient>

    <linearGradient id="snoutGrad" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0.3">

      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#584B42" />
    </linearGradient>

    <!-- Unicycle metal & saddle -->
    <linearGradient id="chromeGrad" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#B8C2CC" />
      <stop offset="45%" stop-color="#F2F6FA" />
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#8C98A4" />
    </linearGradient>

    <linearGradient id="saddleGrad" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#D94336" />
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#99231B" />
    </linearGradient>

    <!-- Bottle gradients -->
    <linearGradient id="greenBottle" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1E8449" />

      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#145A32" />
    </linearGradient>

    <linearGradient id="amberBottle" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">

      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#7E5109" />
    </linearGradient>

    <linearGradient id="rubyBottle" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#922B21" />
      <stop offset="40%" stop-color="#E74C3C" />
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#641E16" />
    </linearGradient>

    <!-- Reusable bottle shape centered at (0, 0) -->
    <g id="bottleShape">
      <!-- Cork -->
      <rect x="-3.5" y="-26" width="7" height="5" rx="1.2" fill="#C99A6B" stroke="#7E5734" stroke-width="0.9" />
      <!-- Body (fill inherited from parent) -->
      <path d="M -4.2,-21 L 4.2,-21 L 4.2,-12 C 4.2,-7 9.5,-5 9.5,2 L 9.5,19 C 9.5,22.5 7,24 0,24 C -7,24 -9.5,22.5 -9.5,19 L -9.5,2 C -9.5,-5 -4.2,-7 -4.2,-12 Z" stroke="#2C241E" stroke-width="1.3" stroke-linejoin="round" />
      <!-- Neck ring -->
      <rect x="-5" y="-21.5" width="10" height="2.6" rx="1.2" fill="inherit" stroke="#2C241E" stroke-width="1" />
      <!-- Cream vintage label -->
      <rect x="-8.4" y="3" width="16.8" height="11.5" rx="1.5" fill="#FFF8E7" stroke="#C8B48A" stroke-width="0.8" />
      <line x1="-5.5" y1="7" x2="5.5" y2="7" stroke="#B58E58" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" />
      <line x1="-3.5" y1="10.8" x2="3.5" y2="10.8" stroke="#D1B280" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-linecap="round" />
      <!-- Glass highlight -->
      <path d="M -5.8,1 C -5.8,-3.2 -2.2,-6 -2.2,-11 L -2.2,-18" fill="none" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.65" />
      <line x1="-5.8" y1="16.5" x2="-5.8" y2="20" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.55" />
    </g>

    <clipPath id="groundClip">
      <rect x="0" y="465" width="640" height="55" />
    </clipPath>
  </defs>

  <!-- Background sky -->
  <rect width="640" height="465" fill="url(#skyGrad)" />

  <!-- Subtle circus tent rays -->
  <g opacity="0.14" fill="#E07A5F">
    <polygon points="320,465 0,0 95,0" />
    <polygon points="320,465 190,0 280,0" />
    <polygon points="320,465 360,0 450,0" />
    <polygon points="320,465 545,0 640,0" />
  </g>
  <rect width="640" height="465" fill="url(#spotGrad)" />

  <!-- Top circus bunting -->
  <g>
    <path d="M -10,12 Q 115,58 245,14" fill="none" stroke="#8C5A3C" stroke-width="2" />
    <polygon points="18,22 44,30 26,46" fill="#E74C3C" />

    <path d="M 410,10 Q 530,54 650,14" fill="none" stroke="#8C5A3C" stroke-width="2" />
    <polygon points="424,16 450,24 434,40" fill="#3498DB" />
    <polygon points="462,27 490,32 474,49" fill="#E74C3C" />
    <polygon points="502,34 530,36 516,54" fill="#F4D03F" />
    <polygon points="542,35 570,32 558,51" fill="#2ECC71" />
    <polygon points="582,30 610,24 600,43" fill="#E74C3C" />
  </g>

  <!-- Ground stage -->
  <rect x="0" y="465" width="640" height="55" fill="url(#groundGrad)" />
  <line x1="0" y1="465" x2="640" y2="465" stroke="#8F552E" stroke-width="3" />

  <!-- Scrolling ground motion lines -->
  <g clip-path="url(#groundClip)" opacity="0.35" stroke="#7A4421" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-linecap="round">
    <g>
      <line x1="30" y1="482" x2="88" y2="482" />
      <line x1="170" y1="496" x2="215" y2="496" />
      <line x1="295" y1="480" x2="360" y2="480" />
      <line x1="440" y1="502" x2="500" y2="502" />

      <animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="translate" from="0 0" to="-640 0" dur="3.2s" repeatCount="indefinite" />

  </g>

  <!-- Ground shadow under unicycle -->
  <ellipse cx="320" cy="472" rx="64" ry="9" fill="#6E3B1B" opacity="0.32">
    <animate attributeName="rx" values="64;59;64;68;64" dur="1.6s" repeatCount="indefinite" />

    <animate attributeName="d" dur="1.6s" repeatCount="indefinite"

    <animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="translate" dur="1.6s" repeatCount="indefinite"
      values="298 405; 304 389; 320 383; 336 389; 342 405; 336 421; 320 427; 304 421; 298 405" />

  <!-- ==================== UNICYCLE ==================== -->
  <g id="unicycle">
    <!-- Spinning spokes & rim -->
    <g>
      <g stroke="#BFC9CA" stroke-width="2">
        <line x1="320" y1="352" x2="320" y2="458" />
        <line x1="267" y1="405" x2="373" y2="405" />

      <animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="rotate" from="0 320 405" to="360 320 405" dur="1.6s" repeatCount="indefinite" />
    </g>

    <!-- Rim & Rubber Tire -->
